chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfaly, from Ziyad ibn Amr al-Ju'fy, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has assigned an Angel to construction, saying to the one who raises a roof above eight cubits: 'Where are you intending (to go to), O wicked one?'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the eight-cubit height limit for roofs in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the architectural limit of eight cubits to divine oversight by a specific angel who calls out to builders as 'wicked' (*fasiq*) for exceeding it. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing urban planning and structural dimensions as subjects of spiritual accountability, where physical height serves as a metaphor for pride or transgression against natural order.
